reversible cross-linking of polymer coronal regions in micelles and hierarchical architectures can be achieved using Pt(0) complexes.
reversible cross-linking of PFS-b-PI block copolymer cylindrical micelles can be induced through Pt(0) olefin coordination.
reversible cross-linking of polymer coronas in micelle, block comicelle, and hierarchical architectures is possible through Pt(0) coordination of olefins.

the use of reversible Pt(0)-coordination cross-linking as a new method for controlling the self-assembly and disassembly of block copolymers.
the development of a reversible cross-linking strategy for PI coronal domains of micellar structures, block comicelles and hierarchical scarf structures.
the use of Pt(0)-coordination to reversibly cross-link the PI coronas of block copolymer assemblies and homopolymer solutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reversible Pt(0)-mediated cross-linking of olefin-containing polymers is a powerful and versatile tool for the modification of polymer structures.
the reversible cross-linking of Pt(0)-containing polymers can be achieved through Pt(0) coordination of alkene moieties.
reversible PI cross-linking through platinum-alkene coordination provides a new and powerful tool for the manipulation of block copolymer nanostructures.

Pt(0) coordination can be used as a general method to cross-link PI coronal regions in block copolymer architectures.
reversible PI cross-linking can occur via both Pt(0)-allyl and Pt(0)-Pt(II) coordination, with the latter being the most efficient and selective method for PI cross-linking.

reversible cross-linking of polymer coronal regions can be used to tune the stability and morphology of block copolymer assemblies and hierarchical architectures.
reversible Pt(0)-based cross-linking of olefin-containing polymers is possible, providing an alternative to traditional metal-catalyzed hydrosilylations.
reversible PI cross-linking through coordination of the Pt(0) species can be used as a new tool for the manipulation of block copolymer self-assembled architectures.
